questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My father give up/smoking when/I was twelve / years old.
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part mentioned in option (a).

'Father' is a singular noun which cannot be followed by the plural verb 'gives'. Also, 'when I was twelve years old' implies that the father stopped smoking in the past.

So, 'give' should be replaced with the past tense form of the verb, i.e., 'gave'.

The correct sentence is: My father gave up smoking when I was twelve years old.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Directions : Read the given passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

The discovery of a new bird species has sparked excitement among ornithologists and bird enthusiasts worldwide. The bird, named the Sapphire-winged Warbler, discovered in a remote tropical island's rainforests, is a unique bird with vibrant blue feathers and a distinctive melodic song. Birdwatchers and nature enthusiasts have been flocking to the island in hopes of catching a glimpse of this elusive and captivating creature. The discovery of the Sapphire-winged Warbler highlights the importance of preserving and protecting habitats. Amidst the excitement surrounding the discovery of the Sapphire-winged Warbler, researchers have embarked on a mission to uncover the bird's migratory patterns. Equipped with satellite tracking devices, they aim to trace the remarkable journey of this species across vast distances. By unravelling its migratory routes and stopover locations, scientists hope to gain insight into the challenges the Sapphire-winged Warbler faces during its arduous travels. The local community on the tropical island has embraced the newfound avian resident with great enthusiasm. Efforts are underway to raise awareness about the importance of conservation and to create protected areas that ensure the continued existence of this exquisite species.

Based on the given passage, which of the following inferences can be made?
options_en: The Sapphire-winged Warbler is an aggressive and territorial bird species.
Conservation efforts are solely focused on protecting the Sapphire-winged Warbler.
The discovery of the Sapphire-winged Warbler has sparked global interest in birdwatching.
The scientific community has lost interest in studying avian species.
questions.solution_en:
Refer to the following sentence from the passage - "Birdwatchers and nature enthusiasts have been flocking to the island in hopes of catching a glimpse of this elusive and captivating creature." From this sentence, it can be inferred that the discovery of the new bird species sparked global interest in birdwatching as many nature enthusiasts flocked to the island the catch the glimpses of the bird.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Nothing in the passage suggests that the new bird species is aggressive. The scientific community rather had more interest as suggested from the following sentence of the passage - "By unravelling its migratory routes and stopover locations, scientists hope to gain insight into the challenges the Sapphire-winged Warbler faces during its arduous travels."

The passage mentions that conservation efforts are focused on this exquisite species, but it does not imply that they are solely focused on this species.

questions.q_en:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select the option that has an error.

The professor instructed the students to submit their final essays to their teaching assistant and myself by the end of the day.
options_en: to their teaching assistant and myself
questions.solution_en:
This question tests the incorrect use of a reflexive pronoun. "Myself" should only be used reflexively (I hurt myself) or for emphasis (I myself will do it). It cannot be used as an object in a prepositional phrase. The correct objective pronoun is "me." The correct phrasing is "...to their teaching assistant and me."

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The clothes can be washed by you later.
options_en: You will wash the clothes later.
You can wash the clothes later.
You have to wash the clothes later.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the helping verb 'be' and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below.

Modal verbs can be identified by the following:
Can
Could
May
Might
Shall
Should
Will
Would
Must

In Passive voice, the format is: Subject (Objective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Object (Subjective case).

Thus, the format of sentences containing Modal verbs in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

For example: This may be done by you. (Passive Voice)

You may do this. (Active Voice)

From the given options, the sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions for Active voice is option (b) "You can wash the clothes later."

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Some parts of a sentence have been jumbled up, and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

Embracing acceptance

P) cultivates a culture of openness and tolerance

Q) for who they are,

R) that fosters a community

S) where people are embraced

regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence is PRSQ. Part P introduces the result or outcome of "Embracing acceptance." It describes what happens as a consequence of embracing acceptance, which is the development of a culture characterised by openness and tolerance. Part R connects to the previous part by explaining the purpose or impact of the culture of openness and tolerance mentioned earlier. It states that this culture serves as a foundation or environment that supports the creation or development of a community. Parts S and Q further explain the nature of the community. They describe that in the community, people are welcomed or accepted for who they are. This implies that people are accepted as it is, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity. The correct sequence (PRSQ) maintains a logical flow in the sentence structure by first introducing the result of embracing acceptance (cultivating openness and tolerance), explaining how this culture fosters a community, and finally describing the inclusive nature of that community where individuals are embraced regardless of their background or beliefs. This arrangement forms a coherent and meaningful sentence describing the positive effects of embracing acceptance.

The sentence formed is: Embracing acceptance cultivates a culture of openness and tolerance that fosters a community where people are embraced for who they are, regardless of their background, beliefs, or identity.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

The mayor _____ plans to revitalize the downtown area and _____ more businesses.
questions.solution_en:
According to the subject-verb agreement rule, we cannot use the plural verb 'revitalize' (imbue (something) with new life and vitality) with the singular subject 'mayor'. So, option (b) is eliminated. The present participle verb 'attracting' doesn't fit in the first position as it requires a helping verb before it which is not there. So, option (c) is eliminated. Revitalizing plans don't 'annihilate' [destroy] businesses. So, option (d) is eliminated.

Among the given options, option (a) contains the correct combination of words.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The mayor announced plans to revitalize the downtown area and attract more businesses.

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Rita is the shorter in the entire school.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence compares Rita with everyone else at the school.

The sentence has used the article 'the', which is used before superlative degree. Also, the phrase 'entire school' indicates that more than two people have been compared.

Therefore, the comparative adjectives do not fit here, which makes options a) and d) incorrect. Thus, a substitution is required. Option b) is contextually incorrect as it does not meaningfully qualify the noun 'Rita'. It should be noted that height is not qualified using the adjective 'long'. Option c) is in superlative degree.

Therefore, the correct answer is option c).

Note:

The Positive Degree of an Adjective is the Adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of the quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Definite and indefinite articles: In English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to, or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

The complete sentence is: The intern's sloppy work on the final report was full of careless errors and typos.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The damp weather is synonymous with a host of diseases and skin problems, which varies according to the many skin types.
questions.solution_en:
In the given sentence, 'which' is a relative pronoun. The verb that follows a relative pronoun is used according to the antecedent that precedes the relative pronoun. In this case, 'skin problems' is the antecedent. Since it is a plural noun, we cannot use the singular verb 'varies'. So, the underlined part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect. Option (a) is also incorrect for the same reason. 'Accordingly' is an adverb. Example - "The boss told me how to do the project, and I acted accordingly." We cannot use the preposition 'to' after 'accordingly'. So, option (b) is also eliminated. Among the given options, option (d) is the correct choice.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) ancient libraries like Alexandria

(Q) preserving knowledge for future generations

(O) housed vast collections of scrolls,

(R) across diverse cultures
questions.solution_en:
The sentence logically begins with part (P) "Ancient libraries like Alexandria", which introduces the subject of the sentence. This subject requires a verb to explain what these libraries did.

Part (O) "housed vast collections of scrolls," provides this verb ("housed") and its object ("vast collections of scrolls"), naturally following (P). So far: "Ancient libraries like Alexandria housed vast collections of scrolls,".

Part (Q) "preserving knowledge for future generations" is a participial phrase that describes the purpose or result of housing these scrolls. It explains what the action in (P) and (O) achieved.

Finally, part (R) "across diverse cultures" is a prepositional phrase that further modifies "knowledge" or "generations," indicating the scope or reach. It provides additional context to (Q).

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is POQR.

The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Ancient libraries like Alexandria housed vast collections of scrolls, preserving knowledge for future generations across diverse cultures.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank(s).

____ ants and their friends were going to _____ temple.
questions.solution_en:
The first blank is followed by a plural noun 'ants' and so either the definite article 'the' or a determiner that denotes a plural noun is the correct choice for that blank. The second blank is followed by a common noun 'temple' and it can be indicated by the indefinite article 'a'. Among the options, 'an' in options (a) and (d) and 'a' in option (c) for the first blank indicate a singular noun, in contrast to the plural noun 'ants'. So, the options are negated. 'A few' is a determiner that indicates more than one but not a large quantity of an object. This suitably quantifies the noun 'ants'. Similarly, 'a' suggested for the common noun 'temple' is also the correct fit.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

Determiner: A modifying word that determines the kind of reference a noun or noun group has, for example, 'a', 'the', 'every', 'much', 'many', etc.
